family.tagline: Two people, one Companion Core, and a cottage full of drawings.
family.story: Malia draws botanical prints in the sunroom, and Sione builds websites for clients from the study. The print shop and the web work share one Companion Core in a cottage at Rookbeck.

companion.name: Marigold
companion.job: Drafts replies to print customers from the notes Malia sends it.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Malia reads and sends every message.

companion.name: Chai
companion.job: Walks the pages of Sione’s draft sites and lists what needs fixing.
companion.limits: Lists only. Sione reads every list and makes the changes.

popup.title: Malia clears the writing desk
popup.body: The Companion Core arrives as a parcel on the stone steps. Sione carries it to the Study, where Malia clears the writing desk.

popup.title: Unbox the Companion Core
popup.body: Inside: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. Malia sets the Core on the desk while Sione reads the guide.

popup.title: Plug it in
popup.body: Sione plugs in the cable, and Malia presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Join it from a phone
popup.body: On his phone, Sione joins the Core’s own network, then chooses the home network.

popup.title: Pick the first agents and apps
popup.body: In the Companion Hub store, Malia and Sione pick Hermes and OpenClaw, then add Inkscape and WordPress. They name the agents Marigold and Chai.

beats.capability: an agent with browser automation and tool use, running in a sandboxed app on your Core

popup.title: Chai says hello
popup.body: Sione greets Chai, the agent he named. Chai answers from the Core on the desk.

say.speaker: sione
say.text: Good morning, Sione. This is Chai. What shall we open first?

beats.capability: run a website or blog on your own Core

popup.title: Sione shapes a cheesemaker’s pages
popup.body: A cheesemaker wants new pages by Friday, so Sione builds them in WordPress on the Core. Pictures and drafts sit there while he works.

beats.capability: chat with models running on your own Core, from any browser

popup.title: Sione asks the model for help
popup.body: One Grist formula in a client’s price list will not add up. Sione asks a model on the Core, through Open WebUI, and the question stays there by default.

beats.capability: an agent with browser automation and tool use, running in a sandboxed app on your Core

popup.title: Chai finds the loose ends
popup.body: Pictures without a description turn up on the cheesemaker’s draft pages. Chai walks them in WordPress and lists the gaps, and Sione reads the list before he changes anything.

say.speaker: sione
say.text: Here is the list. Please read it before you change a page.

beats.capability: track every subscription you pay for and get a reminder before it renews

popup.title: Malia asks about the font licence
popup.body: Malia asks when the font licence renews. Sione looks it up in Wallos by the fireplace. The date sits on the Core, with a reminder before it.

beats.capability: design a Home Assistant dashboard by dragging widgets, with no YAML

popup.title: Sione joins two rooms of lights
popup.body: Rain sends Sione to the sofa. He drags the sunroom lights and the living-room floor lamp onto one GlassHome dashboard. The data stays on the home network.

beats.capability: take notes and keep to-dos that sync across your devices through your own server

popup.title: Malia notes when the ferns unfurl
popup.body: Tea beside her, Malia writes down when the ferns unfurled. The notes sync to Joplin Server on the Core, so her other devices find them there.

beats.capability: stream your own movies, shows and music to every screen in the house

popup.title: Malia puts summer on the TV
popup.body: Last summer’s rowboat videos fill the TV while Malia and Sione share the sofa. Jellyfin plays them from a folder on the Core.

beats.capability: track the pantry, shopping lists, recipes, chores and household habits in one place

popup.title: Malia adds jasmine to the list
popup.body: The tea canister is nearly empty, so Malia adds jasmine tea to the list in Grocy. The pantry count stays on the Core by default.

beats.capability: track the pantry, shopping lists, recipes, chores and household habits in one place

popup.title: Sione checks the flour first
popup.body: Before he bakes coconut buns at the range, Sione checks the flour count in Grocy. The count lives on the Core, next to the recipe.

beats.capability: lists, boards and calendars for tasks, with reminders and recurring jobs

popup.title: Malia and Sione plan studio day
popup.body: The open studio is Saturday, so Malia and Sione plan it on a Vikunja board at the farmhouse table. Vikunja keeps the jobs and their reminders on the Core.

beats.capability: connect your apps with workflows, with the data staying on your Core

popup.title: Sione’s workflow writes the packing list
popup.body: Prints wait on the farmhouse table, and the packing list is already written. Sione’s n8n workflow turns order emails into lines on the Core, with no connector service between.

beats.capability: draw logos, diagrams and line art as vector graphics, in your browser

popup.title: Malia inks a pencil fern
popup.body: A pencil fern on the easel becomes clean lines in Inkscape. Malia saves the file to a folder on the Core, beside her earlier prints.

beats.capability: run a website or blog on your own Core

popup.title: Malia captions the columbines
popup.body: The columbines on the catalogue page still need captions. Malia types them at the bistro table in WordPress, and the draft waits on the Core until she is happy.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Marigold drafts, Malia sends
popup.body: A customer asks which print suits a narrow hall. Marigold drafts a reply from the notes Malia connected to Companion Memory. Malia reads it and sends it herself.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

beats.capability: back up, search and organise your family photos and videos

popup.title: Malia photographs the garden beds
popup.body: A new planting fills the garden beds, and Malia photographs it for her next print. Immich backs the pictures up to the Core and sorts them, slowly at first.

popup.title: The cottage shares one Companion Core
popup.body: Drawings, draft sites and the pantry list sit on one Companion Core in the cottage.

closing.body: Your drawings, draft sites and shopping list can run on a Companion Core at home. Browse the Companion Hub store and pick your first apps.

notes: The spec has no bedroom: nobody is shown asleep, every beat is daytime.
The Study has no desk item in the spec (the Core stands on its own writing desk), so Sione’s desk beats anchor on the core, the room and the fireplace.
WordPress beats stay on the Core and the home network: no beat says a client or customer can reach a site from outside, and no beat sells from a shop page.
Hermes (Marigold) is the first Hermes beat at sunroom-reply and carries the chat-service note; Chai is OpenClaw and opens only apps on the Core.
Companion Memory is named once, in the film beat sunroom-reply; only the notes Malia connected are claimed, nothing else.
Every app used has a QA screenshot, so reviewed.json needs no entry for tuala.
GlassHome and Jellyfin stay on the home network; no beat says the lights or the TV need no cloud account.
The garden beds hold no alliums in the spec (they are on the sunroom roof), so the garden beat says only a new planting.
